objectives.title: Make stepping off the boat and walking onto the quay smooth
objectives.why_score: Named a must by the creator, and it is the player's first moment in the second half of the slice. Not 9 because a snag or gap here breaks the experience on every playthrough.
objectives.detail: Play the exact sequence: boat auto-docks in the DOCK_PORT zone, Q steps ashore, the player walks to the quay and on to the burner. Measure: gap and height between the boat deck, the quay edge and the first walkable surface, the player step-up and floor-snap limits from the player movement spec, camera behaviour during the step, and whether the boat ever moves under the player. Add tools/test_disembark.gd to automate it headless with the Player capsule, and repeat it several times because arrival flakiness has bitten this project before. Work with the Experience agents (Player Movement and QA) and the World crew's dock-zone spec.
acceptance: tools/test_disembark.gd exists and passes 8 of 8 consecutive runs
no snag, no floating step, no camera jump when stepping ashore
the creator walks it and signs it off

checks.note: Creator plays the crossing and steps ashore.

objectives.title: Integrate the port seamlessly into the cliffside
objectives.why_score: Named a must by the creator. Not 9 because a visible seam between port and cliff is seen on both crossings and on the walk up.
objectives.detail: The quay is three instances of saltgate_quay.glb (Saltgate, SaltgateWest, SaltgateEast) set against the cliff modules. Agree the joint with the Cliffside agent in GERFramework/contracts/port_cliff_joint.md, then build the port side: quay stone runs into and under the cliff base, a retaining wall or rock outcrop hides the junction, the stair and ramp start at the same material as the cliff, and the waterline edge is one continuous rock-and-stone line. No floating edge, no gap you can see light through, no visible instance boundary between the three quay copies.
acceptance: contract file exists and is met by both agents
no gap, floating edge or material break between port and cliff from the boat, the quay and the walkway
no visible boundary between the three quay instances

objectives.title: Audit the quay and dock meshes for empty, hollow and holed geometry, then repair
objectives.why_score: Same quality bar as the island and cliffs; the huts are where hollow interiors show. Not 10 because the baseline meshes audit clean.
objectives.detail: Baseline: saltgate_quay.glb (30.9 MB, 249k triangles, one mesh) and dock_harbour.glb audit clean with 0 hole loops. dock_landing.glb is 25.6 MB. Re-run after every change. Because the quay is one baked mesh, hollowness shows as open doorways and windows with nothing behind them, which the audit cannot detect; that is covered visually in SLT-04.
acceptance: zero empty meshes and zero hole loops on every Saltgate and dock mesh in use

objectives.title: Inventory and polish the huts, warehouses and port structures
objectives.why_score: Named by the creator. Not 10 because it depends on the scope decision SLT-05; the GDD keeps the Saltgate minimal until the prototype is complete.
objectives.detail: saltgate_quay.glb is a single 249k-triangle mesh, so individual huts cannot be edited as they are. Inventory what is in it (huts, warehouses, piers, cranes) into Assets/Models/saltgate/saltgate_inventory.json with bounds, then polish in the cheapest order: material and texture passes (salt crust, rot, moss), closing open doorways and windows with dark inset cards so nothing reads as a hollow shell, adding broken shutters, boarded windows and rusted fittings as small props, and tattered amber-and-gold flags per the lore. Splitting the mesh into per-structure pieces or regenerating individual huts through FAL is a cost and scope decision for the creator (SLT-05), not an assumption.
acceptance: saltgate_inventory.json lists every structure
no open doorway or window shows an empty void in a close-up sweep
each hut reads as abandoned 1800s harbour against the concept art

objectives.title: Decide the polish scope: the GDD keeps the Saltgate minimal until the prototype is complete
objectives.why_score: The GDD and Technical Strategy say the Saltgate is minimal until the prototype is complete; this work is the creator overriding or timing that. It gates the cost of SLT-04. Not 10 because there is a safe default.
objectives.detail: Options: (a) polish now, with materials, closed openings and props only, no new FAL generations; (b) polish now including regenerating or splitting huts, which spends credits; (c) wait until the prototype is complete. Huts stay closed shells in every option; enterable interiors are not in the GDD.
acceptance: the creator has chosen a scope
objectives.decision: Polish now (a) without FAL spend, (b) with FAL regeneration or mesh splitting, or (c) wait? Recommendation: (a) now, with (b) offered per hut after you see the result. Also confirm huts stay closed shells.
